sentences.text: ↵We've all been there.

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: You open a test file, expecting to understand what the code does, and instead you're greeted with a monstrosity that makes you question everything.

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: Unit tests are supposed to make our lives easier—they document behavior, catch regressions, and give us confidence to refactor.

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: But sometimes, they become the very thing they were meant to prevent: unmaintainable nightmares.↵Let me share some of the ugliest unit tests I've encountered in the wild.

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: Names have been changed to protect the guilty, but the horror is real.

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: ↵:::danger{title="🔥 The Problem"}↵This test violates the fundamental principle: one test, one concern.

sentences.text: When this test fails, which of the five different behaviors broke?

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: You'll need to debug through the entire method to find out.

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: Tests become interdependent—if user creation fails, everything else fails too, hiding other potential bugs.↵**What it should be**: Five separate tests, each with a clear name describing what it verifies.

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: When testUserDeletion fails, you know exactly where to look.↵:::

sentences.text: ↵:::warning{title="⏰ The Problem"}↵Timing-based tests are flaky nightmares.

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: On a fast machine, 5 seconds might be enough.

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: On a slow CI server under load, it might not be.

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: The test passes locally but fails randomly in production.

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: Developers start ignoring test failures because "it's just that flaky test again."↵**What it should be**: Use proper synchronization mechanisms—callbacks, promises, or polling with timeouts.

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: Mock the async behavior if possible.

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: Never rely on arbitrary sleep durations.↵:::

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: ↵:::bug{title="The Problem"}↵Massive duplication makes maintenance a nightmare.

sentences.text: Update it in 50 places.

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: The setup code is longer than the actual test logic, burying the important parts in noise.↵**What it should be**: Extract test fixtures, use factory functions, or leverage test setup methods.

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: The test should focus on what makes it unique, not repeat boilerplate.↵:::

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: ↵:::question{title="The Problem"}↵What do these numbers mean?

sentences.text: Why is 315 the expected result?

sentences.text: Is the discount 10% or 0.1%?

sentences.text: When this test fails, you'll spend 10 minutes with a calculator figuring out the math before you can even start debugging.↵**What it should be**: Use named constants or variables that explain the calculation.

sentences.text: const decimal ITEM_PRICE = 100m; const int QUANTITY = 2; const decimal DISCOUNT_PERCENT = 10m; Now the test documents itself.↵:::

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: These tests add zero value while increasing maintenance burden and build time.↵**What it should be**: Test your code, not the framework.

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: If you're not adding any business logic, you don't need a test.↵:::

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: ↵:::tip{title="The Problem"}↵Comments that just repeat what the code does are noise.

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: They don't add clarity—they add clutter.

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: If your test needs this many comments to be understandable, the test itself is poorly written.↵**What it should be**: Write self-documenting code with clear variable names and structure.

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: Use the test name to describe what's being tested.

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: Comments should explain why, not what.↵:::

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: ↵:::failure{title="The Problem"}↵This test always passes because it doesn't assert anything.

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: It's a false sense of security.

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: The payment could fail, throw an exception that's caught internally, or return an error—and the test would still be green.↵**What it should be**: Assert the expected outcome.

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: Did the payment succeed?

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: Was the database updated?

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: Did the user receive a confirmation?

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: A test without assertions is not a test.↵:::

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: This test verifies nothing about the actual business logic.

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: It's so isolated from reality that it could pass while the production code is completely broken.↵**What it should be**: Mock external dependencies (databases, APIs, file systems), but don't mock everything.

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: Test real logic with real objects when possible.

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: Integration tests complement unit tests—use both.↵:::

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: ↵:::danger{title="The Problem"}↵Skipped tests are technical debt that never gets paid.

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: "Will fix later" becomes "will never fix." These tests rot, becoming more outdated and harder to fix over time.

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: Eventually, no one remembers why they were skipped or what they were supposed to test.↵**What it should be**: Fix the test or delete it.

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: If it's truly flaky, make it deterministic.

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: If it's testing something that no longer matters, remove it.

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: Skipped tests are worse than no tests—they give false confidence.↵:::

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: What makes these tests ugly isn't just poor style—it's that they fail at the fundamental purpose of testing: providing confidence that code works correctly and documentation of how it should behave.↵Good tests share common characteristics:↵**Focused**: One test, one behavior.

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: When it fails, you know exactly what broke.↵**Readable**: The test name and structure clearly communicate what's being tested and why.↵**Deterministic**: Same input, same output, every time.

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: No flakiness, no randomness, no timing dependencies.↵**Fast**: Tests should run in milliseconds, not seconds.

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: Slow tests don't get run.↵**Independent**: Tests don't depend on each other or shared state.

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: They can run in any order.↵**Maintainable**: When requirements change, tests are easy to update.

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: Duplication is minimized.

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: If you recognize your own code in these examples, don't feel bad—we've all written ugly tests.

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: The important thing is to learn and improve.↵When you write your next test, ask yourself:↵If this test fails six months from now, will I understand why?↵Am I testing my code or the framework?↵Could I delete half of this setup code and still have a valid test?↵Does this test give me confidence that the code works?↵Unit testing is a skill that improves with practice.

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: The ugly tests we write today teach us to write better tests tomorrow.

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: Share your testing horror stories with your team.

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: Laugh about them.

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: Learn from them.

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: And most importantly, refactor them.↵Because the only thing worse than ugly tests is no tests at all.↵:::success{title="✨ The Silver Lining"}↵Every ugly test is an opportunity to learn.

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: Code review catches these issues.

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: Refactoring improves them.

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: And sharing these stories helps the entire community write better tests.

sourceRef.title: Ugly Unit Tests - A Collection of Testing Horrors

sentences.text: We're all in this together.
